blocking.issue: Partly resolved. Usage-missing attempts now pay all of R, which matches pack 8.9. The overshoot bound was not updated for per-attempt settlement, though. Admission reserves R once, but settlement charges R, or reported usage, for every attempt, and one request can make up to (`retries.attempts` + 1) x candidates attempts. A Consumer with R left in its window can therefore make the operator pay the provider for up to N x R per request, and K concurrent requests overshoot by up to K x (N - 1) x R. The only stated bound is estimate error plus hidden reasoning on `gemini` and `ollama`. Attack (denial of wallet): send prompts that make every candidate fail after the provider starts billing. Examples are a reasoning model that thinks past `perTryTimeout` with no content event, which triggers 'Timeout or stream error before content -> Provider Fallback: Yes', or an Anthropic stream that sends `message_start` usage and then an `error` event. Each fallback bills again beyond the admitted reservation. SM-10 and pack 8.9 promise a bound that this design does not keep.
blocking.evidence: Settlement: "Rows 1 and 2 apply pack 8.9, row 2 per attempt" and "| Attempt reached the provider, no usage read | ... | All of R for that attempt |"; "| Usage reported | Any attempt | That usage, summed over attempts |". Model routing: "a request makes at most (`retries.attempts` + 1) x candidates attempts (lower cap: OQ-ai-llm-gateway-16)". Overshoot bound: "a budget overshoots by at most the sum of input-estimate errors across concurrent requests (hypothesis; SM-10 ...), plus, while OQ-ai-llm-gateway-17 is open, hidden reasoning above C on `gemini` and `ollama`."
blocking.fix: Extend the Overshoot bound with the term "plus up to (attempts - 1) x R per concurrent request, where attempts is at most (`retries.attempts` + 1) x candidates (hypothesis)". On Routes with `ai.token-budget`, make the safe option the default: cap total provider attempts per request at 2 (target) until OQ-ai-llm-gateway-16's attempt cap is registered, and stop Provider Fallback with `RZ-AI-005` once the attempts' summed charge reaches R. Add the per-attempt overshoot to OQ-ai-llm-gateway-15's question, because pack 8.9 and SM-10 must be amended to match.

blocking.section: Security and data residency routing / Data residency routing (last paragraph)
blocking.issue: The Semantic Cache residency rule contradicts the normative rule in Security and identity, and it permits a residency violation (T21). This document routes the embedding call and the cache entries to the serving Node's Region. It then lets a residency-split Route attach one `ai.semantic-cache` Policy per residency class, with an embedding provider in the Node's Region. Security and identity requires each embedding provider to be in the Region of the residency class its `when` selects. It also forbids any request whose class differs from the Node's Region from using the Semantic Cache. Attack or failure: operators steer clients by DNS (pack 8.13), and an EU-tagged partner hits a US Node during failover or through a misrouted resolver. The EU-class `ai.semantic-cache` Policy sends the EU prompt to the US embedding provider and stores the EU completion in the US State Store. The generation candidate stays in the EU, so the operator believes residency held.
blocking.evidence: 06 Data residency routing: "Residency routing covers only the generation provider; the embedding call, Semantic Cache entries, access logs and telemetry follow the serving Node's Region ... Every `ai.semantic-cache` embedding provider MUST be in the serving Node's Region, and a Route whose candidates split on residency MUST guard `ai.semantic-cache` with `Policy.spec.when`, one Policy per residency class with distinct `slot` values". 08-security-and-identity.md Compliance: "Each `ai.semantic-cache` embedding provider MUST be in the Region of the residency class its `when` selects, and a request whose class differs from the Node's Region MUST NOT use the Semantic Cache: it is served uncached or fails closed with an `RZ-AI` code."
blocking.fix: Adopt the Security and identity rule word for word. Each embedding provider is in the Region of the residency class its `when` selects. A request whose residency class differs from the serving Node's Region MUST NOT use the Semantic Cache for lookup or store: it is served uncached, or fails closed with an `RZ-AI` code. Until OQ-ai-llm-gateway-9 supplies the Node Region input that Security and identity names, fail safe: a Route whose candidates split on residency MUST NOT attach `ai.semantic-cache`, and `ruralz bundle audit` reports any that do. Record in OQ-ai-llm-gateway-9 that Security and identity chose option (a).

blocking.section: Unified API / Surface decoder (Strict JSON); Native passthrough (edits table)
blocking.issue: The strict JSON rule compares member names only for exact repetition after unescaping. It does not cover names that differ only in case. The Go `encoding/json` v1 API, which Go 1.27 keeps on top of the v2 implementation, matches struct fields case-insensitively. Provider servers match exactly. Native passthrough reads fields with a decoder but edits bytes in place and forwards 'unknown fields' unchanged, so the decoder and the provider can see different cap and model members. Attack on an `openai` native Route: send {"max_completion_tokens":100000, "MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS":16, ...}. A case-insensitive decoder takes C = 16 and reserves E + 16, and the editor writes C into the member it recognized. The provider ignores the upper-case member and applies 100000. Hidden reasoning is never streamed, and this document says 'only the provider's cap bounds it', so the model bills about 100k reasoning tokens before the streaming guard sees 16 visible tokens. Authoritative usage then settles far above the reservation, and repeating the request concurrently drains provider spend beyond any Token Budget. The same mismatch applies to `model`, `n` and `candidateCount`, and to `stream`.
blocking.evidence: Surface decoder: "Every `request.body` decode that CEL, a Policy or the decoder reads MUST reject invalid UTF-8 and repeated member names at any depth, compared after unescaping, so no reader sees a different `model`, cap, `stream` or MCP `method`." Native passthrough: "Everything else, including unknown fields, key order and cache markers, passes unchanged"; edit "Write C into the cap field; remove other cap fields". Streaming guard: "Hidden reasoning is never streamed, so only the provider's cap bounds it."
blocking.fix: Add to Strict JSON: member names match case-sensitively, byte for byte after unescaping, as `encoding/json/v2` does by default and as `jsontext` tokens allow. Case-insensitive v1 matching MUST NOT be used. Reject with `RZ-AI-002` any object with a member whose name equals a field the decoder or editor recognizes (`model`, every cap field in the Native APIs table, `stream`, `n`, `candidateCount`, `stream_options`, `method`, `params`, `name`) under Unicode case folding but not exactly. Add fixtures for case variants of each cap field on each native API.

non_blocking.suggestion: This document says that `http://` base URLs fail validation for every `AIProvider`, `ollama` included. Security and identity says the opposite: TB-3 is 'else cleartext, reported', and Secrets rule 6 expects a loopback `ollama` behind `RURALZ_FETCH_ALLOW`. Keep the stricter rule, which is safer, but align the two documents through OQ-ai-llm-gateway-16. Also explain how a local `ollama` gets TLS.

Only the request direction has an allow list. Add a response-header allow list, for example `content-type`, `retry-after` and a request ID. Provider headers such as `anthropic-ratelimit-*` remaining counts or organization IDs otherwise reveal account-wide usage and account identity to every Consumer on a shared `AIProvider`, which is a T13 side channel like the cached-token counts already listed.
